vectors.name: text_ascii_min
vectors.comment: Smallest realistic envelope: no replyTo, 4-byte senderId, sequence=1, 2-byte ASCII body 'hi'. This is the vector hand-verified byte-by-byte in the C3-28 spec-stage report.

vectors.name: empty_body
vectors.comment: bodyLen=0 is explicitly valid per ENVELOPE.md ('zero length is valid'); body decodes to the empty string.

vectors.name: body_max_2048
vectors.comment: bodyLen at the exact maximum (2048 ASCII 'A' bytes). Also uses the maximum-length (32-byte) senderId and a present replyTo, so the encoded length is exactly MAX_ENVELOPE_LEN = 2126 bytes -- the concrete instance of the 3+16+16+1+32+8+2+2048 arithmetic in ENVELOPE.md.

vectors.name: sequence_max_u64_accepted
vectors.comment: sequence field at the exact maximum representable u64 value (0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF). The codec accepts any nonzero u64 sequence unconditionally; scope-exhaustion behavior at this boundary is client-layer (CONTRACT.md), not a codec concern -- see ENVELOPE.md §10. This is the ONE decode vector whose sequence is not a small ascending integer, by design.

vectors.name: reject_oversize_body_len_2049
vectors.comment: bodyLen field set to 2049 (one over MAX_BODY_LEN) with ZERO body bytes supplied afterward. A valid SEQUENCE_FILLER precedes bodyLen so this vector isolates bodyLen alone. Proves the bodyLen range check fires before any attempt to read body bytes: this must be oversizeBody, not truncated, even though 2049 body bytes were never actually present.

vectors.name: unicode_mixed_emoji_cjk_combining
vectors.comment: Body mixes a combining-mark grapheme (e + U+0301), CJK characters, and an astral-plane emoji, to exercise multi-byte and 4-byte UTF-8 sequences together.

vectors.name: reject_invalid_utf8_0xff_byte
vectors.comment: Body is a single 0xFF byte. 0xFF is never a valid UTF-8 lead byte under RFC 3629.

vectors.name: reject_invalid_utf8_truncated_multibyte
vectors.comment: Body is 0xE4 0xB8 -- the first two bytes of the valid 3-byte encoding of U+4E00 (0xE4 0xB8 0x80, '一'), with the trailing continuation byte dropped.

vectors.name: reject_invalid_utf8_overlong_encoding
vectors.comment: Body is 0xC0 0xAF: the canonical overlong 2-byte encoding of U+002F ('/'), which a strict UTF-8 decoder must reject even though the bit pattern superficially looks well-formed.

vectors.name: reject_unknown_version
vectors.comment: Single byte 0x02. Version is the first field parsed; an unrecognized value fails immediately (ENVELOPE.md: 'stop'), so no further bytes are needed to prove unknownVersion.

vectors.name: reject_unknown_kind
vectors.comment: version=0x01 (valid), kind=0x7F (undefined). Kind is checked immediately after being read; parsing stops there.

vectors.name: reject_flags_unknown_bit
vectors.comment: flags=0x02: bit0 (replyTo-present) is clear, but bit1 is set. Only bit0 is defined in v1; any other set bit is malformed.

vectors.name: replyto_present_valid
vectors.comment: flags bit0 set; a 16-byte replyToId follows messageId. This is the second vector hand-verified byte-by-byte in the C3-28 spec-stage report.

vectors.name: reject_sender_id_len_zero
vectors.comment: senderIdLen byte is 0x00. Valid range is 1..32; 0 is out of range on the low side. No senderId bytes follow (range is checked before the length is used to read further bytes).

vectors.name: reject_sender_id_len_33
vectors.comment: senderIdLen byte is 0x21 (33 decimal), one over MAX_SENDER_ID_LEN=32. No senderId bytes follow: the range check fires before 33 bytes are ever requested.

vectors.name: reject_sequence_zero
vectors.comment: sequence field is all-zero (0x0000000000000000...00) immediately after a valid, complete senderId. No bodyLen/body bytes follow: the range check on sequence fires before bodyLen is ever read, the same 'range checked before further bytes are requested' discipline as the senderIdLen=0/33 vectors above.

vectors.name: reject_truncated_after_version
vectors.comment: Buffer is exactly one byte: 0x01 (a VALID version). The next field (kind) cannot be read, so this isolates truncated from unknownVersion -- if the version byte itself were invalid this vector would be ambiguous between the two errors.

vectors.name: reject_truncated_mid_message_id
vectors.comment: version, kind, flags=0x00 present, then only 5 of the required 16 messageId bytes.

vectors.name: reject_truncated_mid_sender_id
vectors.comment: senderIdLen declares 4 (in range), but only 2 sender-id bytes are actually supplied.

vectors.name: truncated_mid_sequence
vectors.comment: senderIdLen/senderId are complete and valid, then only 3 of the required 8 sequence bytes are supplied (the leading 3 bytes of SEQUENCE_FILLER_BYTES).

vectors.name: reject_body_len_exceeds_remaining
vectors.comment: bodyLen declares 5 (well within the 0..2048 range, so this is NOT oversizeBody), but only 2 body bytes are actually supplied -- distinguishes this from the bodyLen=2049 vector above, which fails on the range check alone. A valid SEQUENCE_FILLER precedes bodyLen so this vector isolates bodyLen/body alone.

vectors.name: reject_single_trailing_byte
vectors.comment: A complete, otherwise-valid 'text_ascii_min'-shaped envelope with exactly one extra 0x00 byte appended after the body.
